discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 051709
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
109 PM EDT Mon Oct 5 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry conditions are expected through this work week.

- After starting out with slightly below normal high temps,
  highs slightly above normal take over for the end of the work
  week.

- Cold Tuesday morning with lows dipping down to the 30s for
  some areas north of US-6.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 103 PM EDT Mon Oct 5 2026

Surface high pressure moves through tonight and shifts off the east, 
Tuesday. This opens the door for warm advection to be on our 
doorstep. Warm advection often pairs with entering cloud cover, 
usually of the mid to upper cloud variety. This time, both the RAP 
and the NAM are picking up on 850 mb moisture that remains overhead 
for a good portion of the area before some upper moisture pushes 
into northwestern areas. If that 850 mb moisture can condense into 
clouds, that really becomes a problem for creating frost overnight 
tonight because it affects especially those areas that have a chance 
to dip down into the upper 30s. Chances are at about 15 to 25 
percent of less than 38F across parts of St Joseph, Branch, and 
Hillsdale counties of MI. If about 3 hours of such 
temperatures occurs, frost becomes more possible, but today's 
models came in a little warmer making it less possible. Soil 
moisture content is lower across the area that could receive the
frost and therefore, could enhance radiational cooling. If 
radiational cooling is able to take effect because cloud cover 
stays away long enough or altogether and winds slacken enough to
allow decoupling, this frost still occur. It probably stays 
more relegated to outlying areas though. At this point, given
the above combination of factors, have held off with any frost 
headlines. With the warm advection that ensues Tuesday, temps 
are forecast to warm through Wednesday, when mid to upper 70s 
are possible.

A cold front washes out Wednesday to Thursday and brings high 
temps back to the upper 60s and low 70s for Thursday and Friday.
Then, another trough enters the Western US and warm advection 
brings us back securely into the 70s for Saturday with low 80s 
possible on Sunday. The warm front is producing rain in model 
output for Friday night/Saturday morning, but it appears to be 
too dry in our area to see the rain. It's also interesting to 
see that the system in the south that tried to get up to the 
area next Sunday to provide some rain is staying just south of 
the area as the dry air hangs tough. As long as this lasts, it 
could be until the following week before we see any appreciable 
rain.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 1212 PM EDT Mon Oct 5 2026

High pressure will continue to promote VFR conditions, little in
the way of cloud cover, and light winds through the TAF cycle.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Roller
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.text:
SPC AC 051628

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1128 AM CDT Mon Oct 05 2026

   Valid 051630Z - 061200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Organized severe thunderstorms are not forecast through tonight.

   ...Synopsis and Discussion...
   Rather strong west-southwesterly low/mid-level flow will overspread
   the Northeast and northern Mid-Atlantic today as an upper trough/low
   over Quebec moves eastward through the period. While locally gusty
   winds may occur with low-topped convection across parts of New
   England, limited low-level moisture and related meager instability
   will likely hinder an organized severe wind threat.

   Showers and occasional thunderstorms will persist today over
   portions of the Southeast as a slow-moving front remains draped from
   the northern Gulf into southern GA/northern FL. A moist airmass is
   in place south of this boundary, but weak low/mid-level winds, poor
   lapse rates aloft, and effective bulk shear less than 30 kt will
   hamper updraft organization and severe potential.

   Elsewhere, isolated convection may continue today across parts of
   the Sierra into Great Basin, and over parts of the southern/central
   Rockies, as a weak upper trough develops eastward. Elevated
   thunderstorms may also occur late this afternoon through tonight
   across parts of the Upper Midwest. For all these regions, weak
   instability will greatly limit the risk for severe thunderstorms.

   ..Gleason/Chalmers.. 10/05/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 051730

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1230 PM CDT Mon Oct 05 2026

   Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely Tuesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   Strong northwest flow will intensify over the northern third of the
   US behind a departing upper trough over the western Atlantic.  A
   secondary low-amplitude trough over southern Canada is forecast to
   move across the Upper Great Lakes and intensify as is moves into the
   northern US. Cool mid-level temperatures beneath the deepening
   trough could support isolated thunderstorms across the northern
   Great Lakes late Tuesday. Otherwise, the cool northerly flow and
   high pressure over the eastern states will favor drier and more
   stable conditions for much of the region.

   To the south of the surface high pressure, scattered thunderstorms
   will again be likely over the Gulf Coast and into central and
   southern Florida as northeast surface winds push a cold front
   farther south. Severe storms are not expected as lapse rates and
   vertical shear are forecast to remain weak.

   A weak upper trough and a pocket of cooler mid-level temperatures
   moving over the Rockies is forecast to steepen low/mid-level lapse
   rates through the day. While ascent and overall moisture will be
   modest, sufficient buoyancy could support isolated thunderstorms
   over the higher terrain.

   ..Lyons.. 10/05/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 050639

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0139 AM CDT Mon Oct 05 2026

   Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low will be situated near James Bay on Wednesday, with a
   broad upper trough enveloping much of eastern Canada. A strong upper
   speed max and tight midlevel temperature gradient will extend
   roughly from MN to the Great Lakes, with gradual height falls across
   the region. Meanwhile, a southern-stream upper jet will extend from
   the Desert Southwest into TX, and across the Gulf Coast states. Cool
   midlevel temperatures aloft will be prevalent over the Four Corners
   states with -12 C at 500 mb.

   Minimal instability will be present to support any thunderstorms
   from the Great Lakes into the Northeast, despite the cooling aloft,
   as surface temperatures will be relatively cool. A few low-topped
   showers may affect the Lower Great Lakes Wednesday night.

   Isolated thunderstorms will again be possible over the FL Peninsula,
   as a front and surface trough gradually move south. Instability and
   shear will be weak enough to preclude any severe weather chances.

   Elsewhere, daytime heating and the presence of cool temperatures
   aloft will support scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms
   over parts of UT, CO, AZ and NM. Isolated evening/overnight
   thunderstorms may extend into NE, as southwest 850 mb winds develop
   over the central Plains, aiding meager moisture advection. Severe
   storms appear unlikely.

   ..Jewell.. 10/05/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
